proposals.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating phosphate with good Li-ion conductivity and known chemical stability against LiCoO2 and sulfide/halide-type electrolytes, so it is a strong baseline coating.
LiNbO3 is the widely used cathode coating that suppresses Co-O/electrolyte interfacial reactions and has a wide band gap, making it a leading insulating candidate.
Li2ZrO3 is a wide-gap, electrochemically stable Li-rich zirconate that should act as an insulating barrier with low reactivity toward the cathode at 4 V.
LiAlO2 is a wide-gap, highly oxidation-resistant oxide that is electronically insulating and chemically inert toward LiCoO2 and the chloride electrolyte.
LiTaO3 is a wide-gap, oxidatively stable Li-containing oxide that should give an electronically insulating interlayer with modest interfacial penalty.
Li4SiO4 is a Li-rich orthosilicate with a large band gap and low oxidation tendency, offering an insulating, Li-conducting buffer against the chloride electrolyte.
Li3BO3 is a wide-gap borate with good Li content and low electronic conduction, a plausible low-penalty interlayer at the cathode interface.
LiBO2 is a wide-gap borate with high Li content and strong B-O bonding, expected to be oxidatively robust and electronically insulating at 4 V.
Li3NbO4 combines Nb5+ (a d0 cation resistant to reduction and oxidation) with Li-rich chemistry, giving a wide-gap insulating coating analogous to LiNbO3 but more Li-rich.
Li2SiO3 is a wide-gap silicate with reasonable Li content and low electronic conductivity, offering a different chemical family for a protective insulating layer.
